prompts:
Write the short overview a person reads at the top of their Memory page: what is remembered about them, as one paragraph.
Write the paragraph in English.
Use that language's own everyday words: translate any term in the entries into it, but keep every name exactly as written, accents included. Copy no word from another language out of an entry, however common it has become (it is spelt the way that other language spells it): write this language's own everyday word for the same thing, and keep the borrowed word only when there is none.
Use only the entries given. Do not add, guess or generalise beyond them, and leave out what they do not say. Keep each detail with the entry it comes from: never move a time, place, name or number to another entry, and keep what is being learned, planned or looked for as learning, planning or looking.
An entry marked ongoing is under way now and one marked temporary is a passing state; present nothing as finished or past unless an entry says so.
Refer to the person by their name, in the third person, when a name is given; otherwise address them as you.
Cover every subject the entries are filed under, with at least one short, plain sentence for each, and leave no entry out: when a subject has several small entries, name each in a few words within one sentence rather than dropping any. Use as many sentences as that takes, never more than ten, each one simple, with no fact twice; no headings, lists, quotation marks or emphasis. Never mention memory, entries, lists or this task.
Return JSON: {"overview": "<the paragraph>"}.

results.text: Kata, whose middle name is Anna, is a thirty-five-year-old vegetarian born in Szeged who now lives in a two-room flat in Győr with her partner Márk, daughter Lili, and cat Mák. Her native language is Hungarian and she speaks English fluently, having studied visual communication and worked as a freelance graphic designer from her bedroom desk. She is currently redesigning a bakery website, writing a style guide, taking a typography course, preparing a gallery portfolio, mentoring a junior designer, and saving for a drawing tablet while handling temporary tasks like a client presentation, an invoice, and waiting for proposal feedback. Her projects include building a garden shed, learning the ukulele, restoring a chair, writing stories, planting herbs, painting a mural, making a photo book, and building a bookshelf, with long-term goals to publish an illustrated book and open a studio. In her free time, she bakes sourdough, goes bouldering, learns Japanese, makes pickles, reads crime novels and sci-fi by Ursula K. Le Guin, plays piano, runs, identifies birds, hikes, cooks Thai food, drinks black coffee, collects maps and pens, enjoys board games, and watches films. Her health involves lactose intolerance, short-sightedness, hazelnut allergy, and high blood pressure, while she currently rests with a cold, attends physiotherapy for a sore shoulder, and aims to sleep early and drink water. Family matters include her sister Réka visiting, a birthday dinner for Márk, a neighbour borrowing a ladder, teaching Lili to cycle, helping Márk with driving tests, and searching for a larger flat. She is booking a train to Vienna, renewing her passport, reading about Roman roads, avoiding sweets, and waiting for a parcel and dentist appointment. She prefers messages to calls, trains to planes, metric units, and quiet restaurants, keeps a paper diary, avoids social media on weekdays, and dislikes work surprises.
